name: ctp-core-iorn-001-measurement
verdict_reason: BLOCKED, and the gate was right: files in the manifest were edited while the run was validating, because the findings were being acted on as they arrived. That is a procedural failure on my part, not a defect in the project or the framework. Both independent reviews of that snapshot completed and both returned fail; their findings are listed below and have been addressed. No run of the expanded snapshot has returned PASS, and this file does not claim one.

local_evidence.note: Run after every fix, on the file contents whose digests are recorded above. These are local runs, not the framework's verdict.

result: 55 of 55 injected defects were caught by the test that claims to catch them
of those, 51 went red on that test's own assertion and 4 went red because the defect made the code raise

executable_test.cause: The shared adapter runs the suite under python -I, which by design ignores user site-packages. NumPy is installed only in the user site, so v1 cannot execute any NumPy-dependent code. A limitation of the shared framework, not a defect in this project.

unsupported_by_v1: Executable tests for any code importing NumPy or SciPy, because the adapter runs under python -I and those live in the user site-packages.
The ctp_core package's own tests, which are pytest-style bare functions; v1 accepts standard unittest only. They are run separately and recorded above.

ClinicalEndToEnd, which needs ctp_core and is therefore skipped inside this snapshot. It runs in the repository and in CI, and the injection proof puts the repository on PYTHONPATH so its mutations exercise it. run_aif.main has no end-to-end coverage at all.
Figure rendering, DICOM geometry and Hounsfield-unit checks, and any visual acceptance. These remain project-specific work and are not covered here.
what_the_rounds_found: Round 1 (ctp_measure only): three implementation defects -- curve_area clipped before integrating; hemispheres used banker's rounding; the enforced domain had no lower bound on the arterial area. Both reviews then returned pass.

Round 2 (drivers added): seven defects. The figure-case gate counted directories rather than comparisons; run_clinical applied one series' time axis to the other unchecked; reference maps were ordered by file name against volumes ordered by slice location; duplicate files could silently overwrite a slice; a pooled stratum was written against amendment 5; the two screens' thresholds had drifted while a test called them identical; run_aif had no population gate.

Round 3: seven more. Either map clipping was reported as both saturating; acquisition numbers were discarded; a non-finite slice position defeated the new position check; the reference gate compared the result against its own input; the strata dropped a case at the boundary; the ctp_measure docstring claimed the drivers hold no arithmetic, which was false; and every driver rebound sys.stdout so no entry point could be called from a test.

Round 4: three defects and the sampling rule's justification. The precision claim was wrong in three independent ways, the real standard error of a hemispheric difference is 0.23 to 0.79 s, and part of the agreement with the reference maps was our own sampling noise -- at 2.81 s the fitted path's whole RMSE. The claim that argmax is three times worse was withdrawn and replaced.

Round 5: the finite-population correction was missing (0.77 % at most, no published number changed); the new completeness gate failed open; a test still asserted a withdrawn claim; and a plumbing run could still destroy the published 15-case result.

Across all five rounds the measured values did not move: every driver was re-run after every change, and the figure case, the arterial area ratios, the quantisation floors and all 60 clinical records are what they were. What changed is how one result is stated, and what the code refuses.
one_review_claim_was_wrong: A reviewer gave 2.0 as the positive area of [0, 2, -2, 0] over times [0, 1, 2, 3]. Recomputing by hand gives 1.5: a trapezoid of 1.0, then a triangle of 0.5 above the zero crossing at t = 1.5, then nothing. The implementation was right and the test's expectation was corrected instead. Agreement between the two reviewers was not treated as proof at any point.

open_items: No run of the expanded snapshot has returned PASS. The two most recent were BLOCKED because the manifest was edited during validation; the one before returned FAIL on findings that have since been addressed. A clean run on an unchanging snapshot is outstanding.

The framework cannot execute this project's tests at all while NumPy lives only in the user site-packages, so its verdict can never be better than FAIL here without either installing NumPy where python -I can see it or amending the shared adapter.
A partly extracted acquisition folder whose file count happens to divide by the number of time points still yields a wrong expected slice count in run_screen.
On the fitted path the finite-population correction uses the admitted count, which is not a random subset of the drawn voxels, so the standard error is approximate there.
